question: In your multi-agent research system, the synthesis subagent keeps a long findings file in which every topic section ends with the identical status line marking it as unverified. After the document analysis subagent confirms the sources for one topic, the synthesis subagent tries to update the status line in that section only. Edit fails because its anchor text matches several places in the file. Which approach should the synthesis subagent take to make this change reliably?

options.text: Retry Edit with the same status line as anchor text until the change lands in the confirmed section.
options.reason: Edit depends on unique text matching, so the same non-unique anchor text fails again on every retry.

options.text: Use Write to save just the corrected section to the findings file, skipping a Read of the existing file contents.
options.reason: Write is a full file operation, so writing only one section would replace the whole file and lose the other sections; Read must load the full contents first.

options.text: Use Grep to find every matching status line in the findings file and replace the one inside the confirmed section.
options.reason: The guide describes Grep as a tool for searching file contents for patterns, not for modifying files.

options.text: Use Read to load the full findings file, change the status line in the confirmed section, and then Write the complete file back.
options.reason: When Edit cannot find unique anchor text, the guide gives Read of the full file contents followed by Write as the reliable fallback.
